newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah succumbs to liquidity, poll.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah succumbs to liquidity, poll.

text.p: * Indonesian rupiah caves in on flush liquidity, nervousness ahead of election.
* Thai baht steady but soft as dollar/majors rise, funds buy dollars in face of weak Thai fundamentals.
* Malaysian ringgit eases on selling against Singapore dollar and U.S. dollar by U.S. funds.
* Singapore dollar hit by strength in dollar/majors but downside protected by ringgit/Sing sales.
The rupiah gave up some of its recent strength amid flush money market liquidity and pre-poll jitters on Wednesday, a day before Indonesia's general election.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,444.50/45.50 at 0430 GMT against an opening 2,442.0/44.0.

"The market expects the Golkar party to win but the margin of victory will be of interest. Anything less than a 70 percent majority would be negative for the rupiah," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.
Golkar, in power for 30 years, has set a target of 70.02 percent of the vote compared with the 68 percent it won in the 1992 elections.
The dealer said Jakarta parties were seen buying the rupiah actively in early trade as short-dated swaps softened.
But said offshore players, who have been long the dollar for the last month on worries about unrest during the election campaign, were looking to sell around the high of 2,445.25.
A local bank dealer in Jakarta said overnight swaps were in negative territory as the overnight rate had traded as low as 4.5 percent.
"Sentiment is biddish on the dollar. Some players are trying to test the resistance level at 2,445.0. Once it's broken decisively, we are heading for the 2,450.0 level," he said.
The Thai baht was steady but soft in slow trade as the central bank's two-tier money market system continued to dampen activity in offshore markets, dealers said.
They said the baht was trading around the central bank's mid-rate of 25.82, though the dollar looked fairly well bid in overseas markets.
"Funds are still looking to buy the dollar on Thailand's weak fundamentals. They're expecting trading to resume in about a month and they're preparing for that," a Singapore-based dealer said.
He was referring to expectations the Thai central bank would lift a ban, imposed to curb speculative attacks, on lending of short-term baht funds by domestic banks to offshore parties.
The dealer said dollar/baht was likely to trade a range of 25.70-25.90, with fears of central bank support for the baht capping its upside.
"The forwards are still trading at double the levels they were at before the attack on the baht. Funds are still collecting swaps, but in a very discreet manner," he added.
In Malaysia, the ringgit remained under pressure as U.S. funds continued to sell the currency against the U.S. dollar and the Singapore dollar.

Dealers said they expected Malaysian interest rates to return to "normal" levels after sharp hikes recently due to a squeeze on interbank funds after heavy intervention by Bank Negara to stem the ringgit's decline.
"It's no more attractive to hold ringgit with the rates falling," a Malaysian bank dealer said.
The Singapore-based European bank dealer said the ringgit selling appeared to be on the back of capital outflows rather than speculative activity.
"Fund managers have been downgrading their weightage on Malaysia due to the poor performance of the Kuala Lumpur stock market," he said.

He said the dollar would face some selling interest from Malaysian corporates around the 2.5200 ringgit level, while 2.5250 was expected to provide a stiff barrier as this was where the central bank last defended the ringgit.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.5165/75 to the dollar at 0430 GMT.
Across the border, the Singapore dollar softened slightly on gains in the dollar/majors but its weakness was limited by ringgit/Sing selling, dealers said.
They said the U.S. dollar looked well bid by local corporates below the 1.4300 level but it was unlikely to rise above 1.4340 due to the ringgit/Sing sales.
The Singapore dollar was at 1.4310/20 against its U.S. counterpart at 0430 GMT.
-- Reme Ahmad in KL (603-201 4813), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
